subject: Pre-Algebra
description: Number system, intervals, exponents, radicals, factoring, functions, graphs, transformations and polynomials

questions.text: Which of these numbers is irrational?
questions.shortExplanation: √2 = 1.4142… never ends and never repeats, so it cannot be written as p/q.
questions.explanation: An irrational number cannot be written as a fraction p/q of two integers. Its decimal goes on forever without a repeating pattern, like √2 = 1.4142… The others are rational: √25 = 5, 0.75 = 3/4 and −8 = −8/1.

questions.text: Which statement about the number sets is correct?
options: Every rational number is an integer
Every integer is a rational number
questions.shortExplanation: Any integer n can be written as n/1, so it is rational.
questions.explanation: The sets sit inside each other: Natural ⊂ Whole ⊂ Integers ⊂ Rational ⊂ Real. An integer such as 5 can be written as 5/1, which is a fraction, so it is rational. The reverse is not true: 3/4 is rational but not an integer.

questions.text: A laboratory temperature must stay strictly between 18°C and 25°C. Which interval shows this?
questions.shortExplanation: "Strictly between" means neither endpoint is allowed, so both brackets are round.
questions.explanation: An open interval (a, b) means a < x < b, so the endpoints are not included. A closed interval [a, b] includes both endpoints. "Strictly between" tells us 18 and 25 themselves are not allowed, so we use round brackets on both sides.

questions.text: How is x ≤ 3 written in interval notation?
questions.shortExplanation: 3 is included, so it gets a square bracket; infinity always gets a round bracket.
questions.explanation: "≤" means 3 itself is allowed, so we use a square bracket next to 3. The values go on forever to the left, toward negative infinity. Infinity is never an actual endpoint, so it always gets a round bracket.

questions.text: A shopkeeper writes 250 + 450 = 450 + 250. Which property allows this?
questions.shortExplanation: The commutative property says changing the order does not change a sum.
questions.explanation: The commutative property means a + b = b + a (and ab = ba). Only the order of the numbers changed here, not the grouping. Remember that subtraction and division are not commutative: 8 − 3 is not the same as 3 − 8.

questions.text: Which calculation shows that the integers are NOT closed under division?
questions.shortExplanation: 2.5 is not an integer, so dividing two integers can leave the set.
questions.explanation: A set is "closed" under an operation if the answer always stays inside the same set. Integers are closed under addition, subtraction and multiplication. But 5 ÷ 2 = 2.5, and 2.5 is not an integer, so integers are not closed under division.

questions.text: Which statement about absolute value |x| is always true?
options: |x| is always positive, even when x = 0
|x| tells us whether x is positive or negative
questions.shortExplanation: Absolute value is a distance from zero, and distance cannot be negative.
questions.explanation: The absolute value of a number is its distance from zero on the number line, so |x| ≥ 0. It can be 0 (|0| = 0), so "always positive" is wrong. It also hides the sign: |5| and |−5| are both 5.

questions.text: Solve −3x > 12.
questions.shortExplanation: Dividing by −3 gives −4, and dividing by a negative flips > into <.
questions.explanation: Divide both sides by −3: 12 ÷ (−3) = −4. When you multiply or divide an inequality by a negative number, you must reverse the sign. So > becomes <, and the answer is x < −4.

questions.text: Which statement is equivalent to |x| < 4?
questions.shortExplanation: |x| < 4 means x is less than 4 units from zero, so it sits between −4 and 4.
questions.explanation: |x| is the distance of x from zero. If that distance is less than 4, x must be between −4 and 4, written (−4, 4). The "or" form is for |x| > 4, where x is more than 4 units away from zero.

questions.text: Simplify (x³)⁴.
questions.shortExplanation: Power of a power: multiply the exponents, 3 × 4 = 12.
questions.explanation: When a power is raised to another power, you multiply the exponents: (aᵐ)ⁿ = aᵐⁿ. So (x³)⁴ = x¹². A common mistake is to add them and get x⁷; adding is only for multiplying powers with the same base, like x³ · x⁴.

questions.text: Which expression is equal to x⁻⁴ (with x ≠ 0)?
questions.shortExplanation: A negative exponent means take the reciprocal: x⁻ⁿ = 1/xⁿ.
questions.explanation: A negative exponent does not make the number negative. It tells you to flip the power to the other side of the fraction bar (take the reciprocal). So x⁻⁴ = 1/x⁴. For example, 2⁻⁴ = 1/16.

questions.text: Evaluate 8^(2/3).
questions.shortExplanation: Take the cube root of 8 (which is 2), then square it: 2² = 4.
questions.explanation: In a rational (fraction) exponent, the bottom number is the root and the top number is the power: a^(m/n) = (ⁿ√a)ᵐ. The cube root of 8 is 2, and 2 squared is 4. Doing the root first keeps the numbers small.

questions.text: Which radical means the same as 27^(1/3)?
questions.shortExplanation: An exponent of 1/n means the n-th root, so 1/3 means cube root.
questions.explanation: The key rule is a^(1/n) = ⁿ√a. With n = 3 this is the cube root, so 27^(1/3) = ∛27 = 3. An exponent of 1/2 would mean a square root instead.

questions.text: What is √72 in simplest radical form?
questions.explanation: To simplify a radical, look for the largest perfect-square factor (a number like 4, 9, 36 that has a whole-number square root). Here 72 = 36 × 2. Using √(ab) = √a · √b, we get √36 · √2 = 6√2.

questions.text: Simplify √12 + √27.
questions.shortExplanation: √12 = 2√3 and √27 = 3√3, so together they make 5√3.
questions.explanation: You can only add "like radicals", which have the same number under the root. First simplify: √12 = √(4·3) = 2√3 and √27 = √(9·3) = 3√3. Now they are like radicals, so add the numbers in front: 2√3 + 3√3 = 5√3. Simplify first, combine second.

questions.text: Rationalize the denominator of 5/√3.
questions.shortExplanation: Multiply top and bottom by √3; the bottom becomes √3 × √3 = 3.
questions.explanation: Rationalizing means rewriting a fraction so there is no root in the denominator (bottom). Multiply the top and bottom by √3: (5 × √3)/(√3 × √3) = 5√3/3. Multiplying by √3/√3 is multiplying by 1, so the value does not change.

questions.text: What is 1/(2 + √3) after rationalizing the denominator?
questions.shortExplanation: Multiply by the conjugate 2 − √3; the bottom becomes 4 − 3 = 1.
questions.explanation: For a bottom like a + √b, multiply top and bottom by its conjugate, a − √b (same terms, opposite sign). Using (a + b)(a − b) = a² − b², the bottom becomes 2² − (√3)² = 4 − 3 = 1. So the answer is just 2 − √3.

questions.text: Simplify 3(x + 5) + 2x.
questions.shortExplanation: Distribute to get 3x + 15 + 2x, then combine like terms.
questions.explanation: First use the distributive property: 3(x + 5) = 3x + 15. Then combine like terms, which are terms with the same variable and power: 3x + 2x = 5x. The answer is 5x + 15.

questions.text: Simplify 6x⁵ / (3x²), for x ≠ 0.
questions.shortExplanation: Divide the numbers (6 ÷ 3 = 2) and subtract the exponents (5 − 2 = 3).
questions.explanation: Handle the numbers and the variables separately. 6 ÷ 3 = 2. For the variables, the quotient rule says to subtract exponents when dividing the same base: x⁵ ÷ x² = x³. So the answer is 2x³.

questions.text: A student writes −3(x − 4) = −3x − 12. What is the correct expansion?
questions.shortExplanation: The −3 multiplies both terms, and (−3)(−4) = +12.
questions.explanation: When you distribute a negative number, it must multiply every term inside the brackets. (−3)(x) = −3x and (−3)(−4) = +12. Forgetting to change the second sign is one of the most common algebra errors.

questions.text: Simplify 3(x + 4) − 2(x − 5).
questions.explanation: Expand each bracket: 3(x + 4) = 3x + 12 and −2(x − 5) = −2x + 10. Notice that −2 times −5 gives +10. Now combine like terms: 3x − 2x = x and 12 + 10 = 22.

questions.text: A student claims (2x + 3)² = 4x² + 9. Which term is missing?
questions.shortExplanation: (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b², and 2ab = 2(2x)(3) = 12x.
questions.explanation: The identity (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b² has a middle term, 2ab, that students often forget. Here a = 2x and b = 3, so 2ab = 2 × 2x × 3 = 12x. The full answer is 4x² + 12x + 9.

questions.text: Factor x² − 49.
questions.shortExplanation: This is a difference of two squares: a² − b² = (a − b)(a + b).
questions.explanation: x² − 49 is one square minus another square, because 49 = 7². The identity a² − b² = (a − b)(a + b) gives (x − 7)(x + 7). You can check by expanding: x² + 7x − 7x − 49 = x² − 49.

questions.text: Simplify (x² − 16)/(x − 4).
questions.shortExplanation: x² − 16 = (x − 4)(x + 4); cancel (x − 4), but x = 4 stays excluded.
questions.explanation: Always factor first, then cancel common factors. x² − 16 = (x − 4)(x + 4), so the (x − 4) cancels, leaving x + 4. The original fraction is undefined at x = 4 (the bottom would be zero), so we must still say x ≠ 4.

questions.text: Which expression can NOT be simplified by cancelling x?
questions.shortExplanation: In x + 5 the x is part of a sum, not a factor, so it cannot cancel.
questions.explanation: You can only cancel factors (things being multiplied), not terms (things being added). In x(x + 3)/x, 2x²/x and 3x/x the x is multiplied, so it cancels. In (x + 5)/x the top is a sum, so cancelling the x would be wrong.

questions.text: What is the domain of f(x) = √(x − 3) for real outputs?
questions.shortExplanation: The number under a square root cannot be negative, so x − 3 ≥ 0.
questions.explanation: The domain is the set of inputs (x values) that are allowed. For a real square root, the inside must be 0 or more, so x − 3 ≥ 0, which gives x ≥ 3. In interval notation that is [3, ∞).

questions.text: What is the range of f(x) = x² for real x?
questions.shortExplanation: Squaring never gives a negative answer, and x = 0 gives 0.
questions.explanation: The range is the set of all outputs (y values) a function can produce. Any real number squared is zero or positive, so x² can never be negative. Since f(0) = 0, zero is included, giving y ≥ 0.

questions.text: A delivery service charges Rs. 200 for 0 < d ≤ 5 km, Rs. 300 for 5 < d ≤ 10 km and Rs. 500 for d > 10 km. What is the charge for exactly 5 km?
questions.shortExplanation: d = 5 fits 0 < d ≤ 5 because of the ≤ sign, so the charge is Rs. 200.
questions.explanation: A piecewise function uses different rules for different input ranges. At a boundary value like 5, check which condition includes it. "0 < d ≤ 5" includes 5, but "5 < d ≤ 10" does not, so the first rule applies.

questions.text: Which real-life situation is best modelled by a step function?
options: The exact distance a car travels
The exact height of a growing child
Parking charges based on time bands
questions.shortExplanation: Parking fees stay the same within a time band and jump at each threshold.
questions.explanation: A step function keeps the same output over an interval and only changes when a threshold is crossed, so its graph looks like stairs. Parking fees, shipping bands and tax brackets work this way. Smoothly changing things like distance or temperature are not steps.

questions.text: The target temperature is 25°C and the deviation is D(T) = |T − 25|. What is the deviation when T = 20°C?
questions.shortExplanation: |20 − 25| = |−5| = 5, because absolute value is never negative.
questions.explanation: The absolute value function measures the size of an error without caring about its direction. 20 − 25 = −5, and |−5| = 5. A temperature of 30°C would also give a deviation of 5°C, just in the other direction.

questions.text: What is the x-intercept of the line y = 2x − 6?
questions.shortExplanation: Set y = 0: 0 = 2x − 6, so x = 3.
questions.explanation: An x-intercept is where the graph crosses the x-axis, and there y is always 0. Put y = 0 and solve: 2x = 6, so x = 3. Note that (0, −6) is the y-intercept, which you find by putting x = 0 instead.

questions.text: For f(x) = x² − 4, we find f(−x) = f(x). What does this tell us about the graph?
options: It is symmetric about the y-axis
It is symmetric about the origin
It is symmetric about the x-axis
questions.shortExplanation: f(−x) = f(x) is the test for y-axis symmetry (an even function).
questions.explanation: Symmetry means one half of the graph is a mirror image of the other. If replacing x with −x gives back the same function, the left and right sides match, so the graph is symmetric about the y-axis (an even function). Origin symmetry needs f(−x) = −f(x) instead (an odd function, like x³).

questions.text: Compared to y = f(x), the graph of y = f(x − 3) is:
questions.shortExplanation: A change inside the brackets moves the graph sideways, opposite to the sign: x − 3 moves right.
questions.explanation: Changes inside the brackets act on x and move the graph left or right, and they work opposite to what you might expect. f(x − h) moves the graph right by h, and f(x + h) moves it left. Changes outside, like f(x) + k, move the graph up or down as expected.

questions.text: Compared to y = f(x), the graph of y = f(2x) is:
options: Stretched horizontally by a factor of 2
Stretched vertically by a factor of 2
Compressed horizontally by a factor of 2
questions.shortExplanation: Multiplying x inside the function squeezes the graph toward the y-axis.
questions.explanation: When the number multiplies x inside the brackets, the effect is reversed: f(2x) compresses (squeezes) the graph horizontally by 2. f(x/3) would stretch it horizontally by 3. Multiplying the whole function, like 2f(x), is what stretches it vertically.

questions.text: Starting from f(x) = x², what does g(x) = −2f(x − 3) + 4 look like?
options: A narrower parabola opening downward with vertex (3, 4)
A narrower parabola opening upward with vertex (3, 4)
A narrower parabola opening downward with vertex (−3, 4)
A narrower parabola opening downward with vertex (3, −4)
questions.shortExplanation: x − 3 moves it right 3, the minus sign flips it down, and +4 moves it up 4.
questions.explanation: Work through it step by step. (x − 3) shifts the vertex right to (3, 0). The 2 stretches it vertically (narrower) and the minus sign reflects it over the x-axis, so it opens downward. Finally +4 shifts it up, giving a vertex at (3, 4).

questions.text: Which equation shows a vertical stretch by a factor of 2 followed by a shift up of 3, applied to f(x)?
questions.shortExplanation: Multiply the whole function by 2 for the stretch, then add 3 outside for the shift up.
questions.explanation: In the general form g(x) = a·f(b(x − h)) + k, the number a outside stretches the graph vertically and k outside shifts it up or down. So a = 2 and k = 3 gives 2f(x) + 3. Putting the 2 inside, as in f(2x), would change the graph horizontally instead.

questions.text: What is the degree of P(x) = 5x⁴ − 3x⁷ + 2x − 9?
questions.shortExplanation: The degree is the highest exponent with a nonzero coefficient, which is 7.
questions.explanation: The degree of a polynomial is its highest power of x. Do not just look at the first term, because terms can be written in any order. Here the term −3x⁷ has the biggest exponent, so the degree is 7.

questions.text: For P(x) = (x − 2)²(x + 3), what does the graph do at the zero x = 2?
options: It crosses the x-axis in a straight line
It crosses the x-axis with a flattened S-shape
It touches the x-axis and bounces back
questions.shortExplanation: (x − 2) appears twice (even multiplicity), so the graph bounces.
questions.explanation: A zero is an x value where P(x) = 0, which is where the graph meets the x-axis. Multiplicity is how many times its factor repeats. Even multiplicity (2, 4, …) means the graph touches and bounces back; odd multiplicity means it crosses.

questions.text: By the Remainder Theorem, when P(x) is divided by (x − c), the remainder equals:
questions.shortExplanation: The remainder of dividing by (x − c) is simply the value P(c).
questions.explanation: The Remainder Theorem says the remainder from dividing P(x) by (x − c) is P(c). So synthetic division (a shortcut for this division) also gives you the value of the polynomial at c. If the remainder is 0, the Factor Theorem says (x − c) is a factor and c is a zero.

questions.text: Describe the end behavior of P(x) = −3x⁵ + 2x² − 1.
options: Falls on the left and rises on the right
Rises on the left and falls on the right
questions.shortExplanation: Odd degree with a negative leading coefficient: rises left, falls right.
questions.explanation: End behavior is what the graph does far to the left and far to the right, and only the leading (highest-power) term controls it. An odd degree means the two ends go in opposite directions, like a line. A negative leading coefficient (−3) means it rises on the left and falls on the right.
